problem: Depth perception models are trained on non-interactive datasets with fixed camera trajectories, which introduces systematic bias. Existing navigation/exploration policies (coverage, novelty, curiosity, semantic reconstruction) are designed for navigation or mapping and do not collect task-specific data for depth completion.
motivation: How data is collected determines what a depth model learns, yet robot exploration and depth learning have been studied separately. Data collected to reduce photometric reconstruction error is observed to help depth completion directly, so exploration should target the model's own error modes.
key_idea: Train a seed depth completion model on random-agent data, use its photometric reprojection residuals as depth uncertainty to pick frontier targets, and collect data with an A* frontier explorer that prioritizes high-uncertainty regions before training a new depth model from scratch.
insight: On MP3D, existing exploration paradigms (Oracle, Smooth Coverage, Novelty) do not give the best depth-completion data. Directing exploration to high photometric-error regions does, with the ranking DEUX > Smooth Coverage > Novelty > Sem. Rec. > Curiosity for KBNet. The DEUX* rows (models trained on MP3D, zero-shot on HM3D) beat Random-on-HM3D for 3 of 4 models on MAE and RMSE (all 4 on those two metrics), which suggests the collected data is more informative and not just more diverse. Results are reported without seeds or variance.
method: Unsupervised depth completion: h_theta(I, sparse z) is trained with photometric reprojection loss (L1 + SSIM from frames t-1 and t-2), a smoothness regularizer, and sparse-depth L1 for metric scale
Seed model: a depth completion model trained on data from a Random agent, used only to compute residuals; it can be replaced by any pretrained depth model
Depth uncertainty: delta = 1 - exp(-mean L1 photometric reprojection error), a per-frame scalar residual, also defining the reward as its negative
Occupancy map and frontiers: build a 2D top-down occupancy map from predicted dense depth and compute free/unexplored frontiers (Yamauchi-style)
Uncertainty-guided target sampling: sample frontier targets prioritizing regions with high residual, plan with A*, and take random actions to unstick when there is no path

Data pipeline: 500 steps per scene, 400x400 RGB-D, ~1500 sparse points (~1%) sampled by Harris corners to mimic SLAM/VIO, GT dense depth never used for training; then a new depth model is trained from scratch on the collected data

setting.backbone: KBNet, VOICED, FusionNet (unsupervised) and ScaffNet (supervised) depth completion models trained from scratch; exploration itself is a heuristic A*/frontier planner driven by a seed depth model
setting.training_data: Self-collected exploration data in Habitat: MP3D (61 train scenes) and HM3D (800 train scenes), 500 steps per scene per exploration policy; 25 epochs of training
setting.observation: RGB-D frames (400x400) with 6D pose; sparse depth (~1500 Harris points) and monocular RGB used for depth completion
setting.action_space: discrete: forward, turn left, turn right, stop
setting.privileged: Simulator poses and rendered depth used for occupancy mapping; GT dense depth is used for evaluation and by the supervised ScaffNet; the Oracle baseline uses pre-sampled targets

results: With KBNet on MP3D, DEUX gets MAE 121.07 vs 135.85 for Smooth Coverage (the strongest learned baseline) and 147.31 for Oracle. It also wins on most metrics for the other three models. The paper reports average gains of about 19% over Semantic Reconstruction, 18% over Oracle and 48% over Random on MP3D. In zero-shot MP3D→HM3D transfer, DEUX beats Smooth Coverage by 5%.
limitations: Only simulation, only depth completion, with no real-robot deployment; the uncertainty proxy is a simple mean L1 photometric residual
Requires a seed model trained from a random-agent stage and pose/depth-based mapping; HM3D lacks the RL baselines, so it is compared only to Random
Not all metrics improve (e.g. iRMSE for VOICED on MP3D, iMAE/iRMSE on HM3D VOICED); no variance across seeds reported; 500-step budget per scene
builds_on: Ramakrishnan et al. 2021 (exploration benchmark for Habitat)
